newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong to review TV and keep role as media hub.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to review TV and keep role as media hub.

text.p: Hong Kong wants to remain a major regional broadcasting hub and will review its "television environment" to maintain that media strength, the fledgling government said on Thursday.
"We cannot afford to rest on our laurels," said Chau Tak-hay, Secretary for Broadcasting, Culture and Sport, announcing a 1998 review of television developments.

"Hong Kong faces stiff competition from other locations in the region," he told a news briefing on the first official working day of the new Special Administrative Region (SAR) government, which has run Hong Kong since its return to China at midnight on June 30.
Until 1991, Hong Kong's broadcasting market had been simple, with just two terrestrial television stations, each with two channels, and two radio stations, he said.

Now Hong Kong had 40 domestic channels, satellite channels were also receivable in Hong Kong, and delivery methods had broadened, including cable television, and soon video-on-demand through telephone lines, Chau said.
After the government's 1998 review of the television environment, it would look at digital broadcasting.
"In the next few months, we will start to plan the options for digital radio," Chau said. "Thereafter, we shall tackle the introduction of digital television."
He said the government planned to maintain a simple regulatory environment, which maintained standards without interfering unnecessarily with broadcasters' freedom.
